claims.text: Weight gain is an important risk factor for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, certain types of cancers, and premature death.
Being overweight or obese is an important risk factor for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, certain types of cancers, and premature death.

Dietary and lifestyle factors, including sugar-sweetened beverages, poor diet quality, physical inactivity, prolonged screen time, short sleep duration or shift work, and built environment characteristics, play a role in obesity.
Genetic factors predispose individuals to obesity.
Genetic susceptibility to obesity can be attenuated by healthy lifestyle choices.

evidence.description: Long-term NHS research has shown that weight gain and being overweight or obese are important risk factors for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, certain types of cancers, and premature death.
Long-term NHS research has shown that weight gain and being overweight or obese are important risk factors for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, certain types of cancers, and premature death.

The cohorts have elucidated the role of dietary and lifestyle factors in obesity, especially sugar-sweetened beverages, poor diet quality, physical inactivity, prolonged screen time, short sleep duration or shift work, and built environment characteristics.
Genome-wide association and gene-lifestyle interaction studies have shown that genetic factors predispose individuals to obesity...
...such susceptibility can be attenuated by healthy lifestyle choices.

methodologies.name: Narrative Review
methodologies.description: Narrative review of publications from the Nurses' Health Studies (NHS and NHS II) published between 1976 and 2016.
